synthesis: Eight retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. System changes such as removing tests from default order sets produced large and durable reductions, and feedback on clinicians' own ordering reduced testing beyond comparison hospitals. Nurse-led protocol triage was associated with less testing. Education alone faded within a year. Where reported, same-day cancellations and complications did not rise. Clinicians describe habit, fear of blame and default ordering as the drivers, and most patients would accept fewer tests if the reason were explained. The evidence supports a rapid review organised by strategy type, with cancellations and complications as balancing outcomes.
gradeRationale: One controlled before-after study and one interrupted time series with large, consistent effects for system and feedback strategies, supported by a review of mostly weaker studies; moderate certainty that system changes reduce testing, low certainty about balancing outcomes.
summary: Eight records appraised; five claims; overall certainty moderate for reduced testing.
